A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XR-1 research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-world robot evaluations, few-shot adaptation, environmental generalization tests, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds CALVIN simulation results, additional ablations, representation analyses, and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated motion-decoder inputs: v1 specifies language and observations alongside the motion code, whereas v2 permits optional conditions and explicitly uses proprioceptive states in its implementation. The dual-branch UVMC architecture and three-stage framework otherwise remain stable.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds CALVIN D-to-D evaluation, extending coverage to simulated, language-conditioned manipulation using CALVIN's 34-task repertoire. The original real-world embodiments and tasks remain. Identifying XR-D as a RoboMIND 2.0 subset does not establish a change to its represented training data.

E2.justification: The new CALVIN comparison in Table 17 introduces evaluated comparators OpenVLA, Qwen-π0, and Qwen-GR00T, alongside RDT-1B, π0, and π0.5. This adds a distinct comparison suite; comparator membership in the retained real-world and ACT/DP adaptation experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces CALVIN testing on 1,000 five-instruction sequences and new retrieval and controlled-ablation protocols. It also changes Stage-2 from absent to downstream-task training for Exps. 2 and 4–9 in v1 Table 4/v2 Table 3. This is a substantive reported-setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds codebook-size, embedding-dimension, modality-only, shared-versus-separate-codebook, and Ego4D ablations. Appendices G–I add nearest-neighbor retrieval, t-SNE analyses, and baseline/XR-1 failure cases. The earlier cross-embodiment transfer analysis is retained as Table 16, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix G.2 and Table 18 newly summarize normalized nearest-neighbor similarity distributions using modes and averages, extending descriptive statistical reporting beyond success-rate averages. Neither version reports repeated-training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include motion-only, vision-only, and unified-code success rates of 35.0%, 50.0%, and 66.7% in Table 14; Ego4D ablation results of 32.5% versus 38.3% in Table 15; and CALVIN scores of 4.256 for XR-1 versus 3.885 for π0.5 in Table 17. Retrieval statistics and failure findings are also added. Matched original real-world scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G.2 introduces a formal construction of the cross-task retrieval statistic: a pairwise motion–vision similarity matrix, column-wise maxima, and a normalized nearest-neighbor vector. Existing training mathematics is mostly compacted or renotated; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: unified vision–motion codes, heterogeneous-data exploitation, a model-agnostic three-stage framework, and strong performance across six robot embodiments and over 120 tasks. Additional evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of codebook saturation, comparable shared/separate codebooks under alignment, human-video benefits, and action-semantic clustering across embodiments. It also explicitly identifies XR-1's precision failures on tiny screws, adding a concrete applicability limitation absent from v1's discussion.

D1.justification: v2 identifies XR-D's relationship to RoboMIND 2.0, specifies the motion-decoder conditioning used, and documents feature extraction and similarity aggregation for the new retrieval analyses. Existing architecture tables, hyperparameters, hardware, training costs, inference speeds, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CALVIN and RoboMIND 2.0 and connects XR-D to the latter. It removes the Weblab xArm reference by Matsushima et al., replacing the corresponding dataset citations with Oh et al. The broader positioning against action-only and video-only representation learning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental narrative undergo substantial condensation and rewriting. Ablations precede generalization, appendices are reorganized into A–J, and an Additional Analyses section is added. The LLM-writing disclosure is removed and an Impact Statement appears.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to two columns. Figure 2 is redrawn with explicit conditioning and token labels, the ablation table's stage columns are restructured, and existing displays are relocated. New CALVIN, retrieval, t-SNE, and failure-case figures accompany four additional tables.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct vision-only/motion-only and human-video controls despite their importance to its central motivation. v2 addresses these gaps in Appendix D and adds representation evidence, simulation benchmarking, and explicit XR-1 failure cases, substantially strengthening validation and clarity about limitations. These benefits are tempered by absent uncertainty estimates and inconsistent Stage-2 labels attached to identical results in v2 Tables 3 and 15.
